1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night

Rain had been falling on the village of Doldari for three days straight. Kim Haneul's older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and ever since, Haneul had been running the village's little apothecary on her own.
As dusk fell, she shut the outer doors, counted the day's earnings, put out the oil lamp, and climbed the stairs to the second floor.
She had just lain down when urgent pounding sounded at the door downstairs, followed by a man's voice. "Is anyone there?"
At the door stood a young man, drenched to the skin. Blood had seeped through the cloth wrapped around his left arm. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was with the Azure Dragon Society.
"Please treat my wound," Park Junho said in a low voice. "I'll pay you. Would three thousand five hundred nyang be enough?"
From his breast he drew out a letter wrapped in oil paper. "This letter must be delivered to Cheongpungsa by the eighteenth day of the fifth month."
Haneul thought to herself: the neighbors were already green with envy over how well the apothecary was doing, and now, of all things, a strange man comes knocking in the dead of night.
Even so, Haneul took no money for it, saying only, "I'll guide you up the mountain first thing tomorrow morning."
2: As soon as day broke, the two of them set out on the road. Haneul carried a basket on her back, and inside it were rice balls, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain they came upon the old man Lee Youngsoo, chopping firewood. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice. The evening before, he said, three strangers had been at the edge of the village, looking for a wounded young man.
"Haneul, take the side path," said Lee Youngsoo. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul took the lead, planting each step firmly as she went, and Park Junho followed in silence.

At noon the rain stopped and the mountain mist slowly lifted, and the roof of Cheongpungsa came into view in the distance. A nun stood before the temple gate. It was Venerable Jeonghye, the one who received guests at the temple.
Venerable Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal on the envelope, and nodded. "The abbot has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "I owe you my life." Haneul replied with a smile. "Then next time you come, you can at least fix the roof of my medicine shop." Park Junho stayed behind at the temple.
Toward evening, Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home, it was already dark. She lit the oil lamp and sat for a long while behind the counter.
